Wind-flagged Araucaria stand, forty trunks leaning east at fifteen degrees, every branch stripped bare on the windward side and swept into dark blue-green fans pointing downwind, snow packed hard against the lee bark, copper lichen burning small and warm on the lowest exposed root.

Krummholz mat of ancient podocarp, centuries compressed flat across granite pavement, no trunk rising more than knee-height, the whole mass silvered and wind-tortured, snow drifted through its labyrinth in cobalt blue channels, one rust-orange scrub stem catching the only colour in the grey rock field.

Two-hundred-foot Araucaria cathedral, eight trunks black-wet in a cathedral row, boughs sagging under snow loads thicker than the boughs carrying them, the shadow between trunks a deep cobalt trench, low pale sun striking the topmost snow-laden tier white-bright against a slate sky.

The tree-line edge mid-slope, dense dark-needle forest stopping clean along a horizontal band, bare snowfield and fractured rock stretching above it, three solitary survivor conifers standing fifty yards past the line alone, small and dark against the open white, the sky above them empty and hard blue.

Frost-rimed giant podocarp, every needle on its sixty-foot spread furred in hoarfrost crystal, the whole crown glittering under thin winter sun, breath-fog cold condensing visibly at the base, one cluster of old cones showing a faint ochre glow deep inside the rime-whitened branch mass.

Avalanche scar bisecting the slope, a hundred-yard swath of snapped Araucaria trunks silvered and bare, the break-lines jagged at chest height, young conifer seedlings pushing six inches through the snow in the gap, their needles vivid dark blue-green against the white debris field.

Cloud-layer forest, the upper canopy of a podocarp stand piercing a cloud deck at roughly a thousand feet, the top third of each massive trunk and its snow-loaded crown floating in cold white silence above the cloud, the lower forest dissolved entirely, only the emergent tops visible, pale sun striking them from above.

Krummholz field at the true tree-line, ancient Araucaria individuals pressed flat into the rock, their trunks no thicker than a forearm yet four centuries old, ice crystals filling every joint in the mat, one dead stem showing copper-needled rust warm against the surrounding blue-white granite.

Snow-loaded mega-conifer grove, podocarp boughs so deep under load they touch the snowpack below, forming white-roofed vaults higher than the boulders they bridge, the interior dim and cold and blue, icicles six feet long hanging from the lowest boughs, the trunks near-black and dripping.

Wind-flagged stand of ancient conifers, trunks spaced wide across exposed ridgeline, every crown reduced to a wind-combed pennant streaming east, the westward bark pale and abraded, snowpack built in a long hard wedge on the eastern side of each trunk, amber low sun on the far ridge small and precise.

Frost-rimed conifer cathedral, two-hundred-year-old Araucaria with each of its horizontal tiers completely whitened by hoarfrost, the branch architecture rendered visible in white crystal, dark trunk contrasting deep and wet below, low-angle light splitting into prismatic cold sparkle across the top tier, everything breathing cold.

Moss and lichen rock garden under dense canopy, five house-sized boulders in a cluster, their faces furred in frozen dark moss and pale grey-green lichen, meltwater that crept across them overnight now glazed as clear ice sheets, the cobalt shadow under each boulder deeper than the surrounding forest floor.

The tree-line itself on a north-facing slope, the last continuous forest ending in a ragged band of wind-deformed conifers, bare scree and old snowfield beginning above, a single tall podocarp survivor standing sixty yards above its companions in the open, one branch flagged hard to the east, the tree visibly losing.

Avalanche debris field three seasons old, the snapped trunks of a dozen Araucaria laid parallel downslope, bark bleached silver, the root balls of two still standing upright like walls, young conifer regeneration knee-high in the gap, snow compressing it, the scar flanked by intact dark forest on both sides.

Cloud-layer emergence at dawn, the upper forest rising through a cloud inversion, podocarp crowns breaking the cloud surface across a half-mile ridge, each emergent crown catching first pale sun from above, the cloud below smooth and white as packed snow, no ground visible, only dark crown-tips floating in cold light.

Frost-rimed giant at the forest margin, its needles loaded so heavily in hoarfrost the branch tips curl downward under the weight, each cone along the lower branches encased in clear ice, the whole tree ticking and creaking in the morning cold, a small patch of rust-orange lichen on the trunk base warm against all that white.

Wind-flagged conifer pair on an exposed col, two Araucaria leaning in unison at the same angle, their combined branch mass swept into a single downwind flag forty feet long, snow packed dense on every horizontal surface facing into the wind, the rock around their roots bare and ice-polished, dark and cold.

Krummholz ancient mat on a boulder field, the trees so old and compressed their wood is almost stone, no individual trunk distinguishable in the mass, snow filling the interior channels blue-white, the outer edge of the mat wind-blasted bare on one side, a warm copper smear of dying needles at the very margin.

Mega-conifer snow cathedral at dusk, six podocarps spaced like nave pillars, their boughs meeting overhead and loaded with snow so the interior is a vaulted space of hanging white and deep cobalt shadow, the far end of the row catching last pale light, the near end in darkness already, all of it very cold and very still.

Moss boulder garden in a frozen hollow, seven granite boulders each the size of a small house, mosses on their upper surfaces frozen solid and dark grey-green, lichen in pale gold-ochre crescents along the sun-facing edges, ice glazing the lower halves smooth, the canopy above them open enough for snow to have loaded every flat surface.

The tree-line seen from above, standing on bare rock and looking down at the forest canopy below, the tops of the Araucaria stand packed close and dark, then thinning, then individual crowns spaced apart, then a last few solitary trees, then snowfield, the transition spanning two hundred vertical feet of slope, clean and irreversible.

Avalanche scar in fresh snow, the break happened this season, raw wood showing pale cream at the snap points on thirty trunks, the debris buried but the snapped stumps standing in a line, snow already smoothing the rubble below, two surviving Araucaria at the scar edge standing stripped of half their branches, still upright.

Wind-flagged ridge conifer, a single ancient Araucaria on an exposed spine of rock, its trunk leaning five degrees, its entire crown a one-sided flag of dark blue-green needles streaming east, the west-facing bark silver and bare, snow in a hard curving drift at its base, ochre lichen thick on the rock around its roots.

Frost-rimed forest margin, twenty podocarps along the edge of the tree-line each furred tip to base in hoarfrost, the collective effect a white wall of crystal against the dark interior forest behind, low pale winter sun on the outer faces, every needle tip catching light separately, the shadow within the stand a saturated cobalt.

Cloud-layer forest interior, standing inside a podocarp stand that has entered a cloud, visibility dropping to thirty feet, every trunk dripping with cloud condensation running in black lines down the bark, snow on the boughs absorbing moisture and turning heavy, the tops of the trees invisible above, only trunks descending into white silence.
